units.text: INT. AFTER-HOURS WAX MUSEUM - NIGHT
Wax figures stand in half-light: a bishop, a boxer, a singer mid-note.
A janitor's cart is parked by the velvet rope.
JACINTA ROURKE (40s, coveralls, ID badge clipped upside down) mops slowly around the boxer's feet.
Her phone sits on the cart, speaker on.
You're in?
units.name: NILS

units.text: Been in an hour. They never lock the sprinkler hatch.
units.name: JACINTA

units.text: And the display case?
units.name: NILS

units.text: She leans the mop against the boxer.
Walks to the singer's display, a glass cube with a gold microphone inside.
She taps the glass with a knuckle, listening.
Alarm's cheap. Same model as my garage.
units.name: JACINTA

units.text: Don't touch it yet. I want to hear your breathing first.
units.name: NILS

units.text: You're not my doctor.
units.name: JACINTA

units.text: I'm your ride, and I'm eating a sandwich in a freezer truck. Humor me.
units.name: NILS

units.text: She exhales.
He listens.
She takes the microphone cable out of her pocket and holds it up to the light.
He swallows and sets down the sandwich.
Okay. Go.
units.name: NILS
